dimensions.note: One pattern recurs across four independently gated readings and is rival-tested in each: practiced composure and care for others held beside wanted indulgence, self-consciousness about that care and an expressive restraint that practice partly opens. B0221 has her ask to be treated as an ordinary young woman and sometimes childishly (A:P1-2), ask for indulgence (F:P4), value a place through its people (D:P3-4), be angry at her own lapse in caring for the theatre (G:P3) and be unable to put the language of love into words until making for the manager gives a channel (H:P14, P91-100, P121). B0232 case 38 gives a protective warning on behalf of same-age peers (P1-P2). B0237 404000024 has her say this expression may not be like her, then deliver a sustained speech credited to MC practice (P0-6, P17). B0244 adds qualified cooperation framed as not troubling Player (503012301 P20), care for an abandoned cat chosen through reluctance, with her saying she was not adult enough to leave it and accepting the childish label (503012304 P9-13), a resemblance she suggests and then refuses to explain (P12-13), and comfort in company that does not appraise her vocal practice (P18-19). D rather than E because this is distributed, rival-tested support across four readings. Not C because no conditional rule, trigger or state guard is derived, and B0244 explicitly keeps the withheld resemblance from becoming a biography or self-theory.

All four readings forbid ordering the occurrences, and B0244 gives its family no placement relative to Main or other families. Self-reported changes are located but unordered: once satisfied simply to sing, she now thinks about how companions appear (B0221 E:P4); live MC experience has made her more accustomed to speaking before people (B0237 P17); and an exceptional rainy-day rescue has become a daily walking and practice routine before shop opening (B0244 503012304 P5-P16). H and B0244 each track movement within their own occurrence. No development across occurrences is established, and the earlier Murasaki states are context only.

Located register evidence stays local: the address お兄さん for the manager (B0232, B0237), the title 色っぽくしたげる (B0221 B), a formal answer to the composer (H:P1-7), the quoted 昨日ファーブの誕生日を祝ったばかり (B0237 P3), her remark that this expression may not be like her (B0237 P0-6), and B0244's textual observation that she qualifies and bounds disclosure, including declining to explain because saying it would be gauche (503012304 P13). The readings otherwise paraphrase her Japanese. All voice cues (30 in B0221 A-G, 15 in B0237, and B0244's family-wide cues) are unheard, H has no voice fields and B0232 carries no voice.

One ordinary task is enacted in dialogue: the chocolate making in H (P42-82). B0244 503012304 adds an ordinary routine, but only in her first-person account: no school club because she helps at the family shop, usually going straight home, and now a limited interval of cat care, riverbank walks and vocal practice that ends at shop opening (P1-P22). Other conduct is completed only in her words (the pedicure in B0221 B:P4, the coffee in F:P1-2) or reported and proposed (an after-work drink with a soft drink for herself in C, joint cleaning in G, a pedicure-shop outing in B0232 P0, a received party in B0237). Not D because the routine is self-narrated rather than enacted, the single enacted task is a Valentine gift, and no unfamiliar ordinary situation is shown.

Two longer occurrences give other people their own turns, and her conduct differs by counterpart. In B0221 H: a formal reply to the composer (P1-7, P105-108), a peer exchange with Kazumi in which she asks for counsel and records a different taste judgment (P14-39, P42-73, P91-100), and a later disclosure to the manager, who answers (P110-122). In B0244 503012305: a compliment to Honoka repeated over Honoka's protest (P3-P5), a request that Player not tease her, which he denies intending (P12-P13), and a refusal of his cat-visit request on a hypothetical allergy ground, which he accepts (P15-P18); the reading keeps his intent and her received effect separately attributed. B0244 503012301 qualifies her cooperation as not troubling Player (P20). B0232 adds a protective stance toward peers set against the addressee (P1-P2), and B0237 a collective thanks distinguished from a specific credit to the manager (P18-22). D rather than E because recipient differences are located across four readings with real other-speaker turns in two. Not C because the differentiated turns come from two occurrences and no recipient-conditioned rule is derived.

Most interior states are spoken self-reports: anger at her own lapse (B0221 G:P3), hurt at being called delicate (G:P4), concern while waiting (H:P65-73), being moved and unsure what to say (B0237 P0-6), and in B0244 503012304 her account of being unable to ignore the wet cat and finding unintrusive company comfortable (P9-P11, P18-P19). B0221 H:P99-100 adds one parenthesized reader-only thought. B0244 keeps the felt resemblance deliberately closed (P12-13) and treats the cat's liking as her interpretation. One reader-only moment and first-person self-accounts do not support a graded inner model.

Located friction is brief: her command that the manager not run away while she removes his socks (B0221 B:P3), which does not supply his assent; her response to Haru's reported scolding, directed at her own failure (G:P2-3); her objection that being called delicate hurts (G:P4); the warning not to make her peers cry (B0232 P2), which establishes no actual wrongdoing; and two challenges to Player in B0244 503012305, over teasing Honoka (P12-P13) and over bringing the cat (P15-P18), each answered by his own turn and settled locally. Not D because no sustained dispute or escalation with a speaking counterpart is analyzed.

One stated harm-based reason is located: she refuses Player's request to bring the rescued cat to Nanasta because a child with a cat allergy might be affected, and tells him to think before suggesting it (B0244 503012305 P15-P17). The reading treats this as attention to potential effects on others limiting access, with the allergy hypothetical and no holder named. Her protective warning (B0232 P2) and anger at failing the theatre (B0221 G:P3) state a limit and a value rather than reasoning, so they are not cited. Not D because a single short refusal shows no weighing of competing considerations.

Play is located in B0221: a suggestive question redirected to styling the manager (B:P1-2), the sweet-coffee exception (F:P2-3) and calling her own jukebox words youthful (D:P5); and in B0244 503012305, where she calls Honoka's sweets-centred account characteristic and cute and repeats the compliment over Honoka's protest (P3-P5), which the reading calls playful personal appraisal. Each is short. B0232 and B0237 analyze no joking by her.

Each curated unit is complete with exact native review: B0221's eight occurrences including the 132-page H, B0232's three-page message, B0237's 24-page Birthday portfolio and B0244's complete 109-page five-chapter family, in which she speaks in three chapters. Apart from H and B0244 503012305 these are short single-speaker addresses or first-person accounts. The earlier Main, i-n-g and Sub readings (B0039, B0087, B0105, B0140, B0178) are not enrolled, and no performed song, audio, loop movie or runtime was reviewed.

Affirmative local limits are located: she cannot make the language of love click or verbalize what making the chocolate felt like (B0221 H:P14, P91), she skipped the theatre cleaning (G:P2), her own drink would be a soft drink (C:P3), her taste for bitter songs does not predict her coffee (F:P3), she already had friends, seniors, juniors and acquaintances before Nanasta (B0237 P19), she belongs to no school club because of the family shop and usually has no after-school time (B0244 503012304 P1-P3), and she declines to explain the resemblance (P13). Each limit is case-local, so D is not supported.

The readings establish that no total chronology orders the occurrences. The explicit markers are local: self-stated age eighteen (B0221 A:P1), a Valentine frame without year (H), yesterday's skipped cleaning (G:P2), tomorrow's planned outing (B0232 P0), Ferb's previous-day celebration (B0237 P3), a past rainy day and the approaching shop-opening time (B0244 503012304 P5, P20-P22). B0244's chapter order is prospective within its family only.

scenario_readiness.note: Her Japanese is mostly paraphrased, with an address form, a title and a few short quotations, and all voice cues are unheard. H and B0244 503012305 supply multi-speaker structure but little quoted wording. Generated lines would be fluent invention rather than source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not Murasaki's speech.

scenario_readiness.note: Eleven unordered occurrences, two of them with multi-speaker exchanges, with no conditional rules, cannot support a novel context.

One enacted chocolate-making scene with a peer, a self-narrated after-school cat-care routine, completed-in-words pedicure and coffee, and proposed drinks, cleaning and shopping answer bounded canon questions about these occurrences, but give no procedure for an unfamiliar ordinary situation.
One short refusal on a hypothetical allergy ground (B0244 503012305 P15-P17) shows a harm-based reason but no deliberation among competing values; simulating her ethical reasoning would be invention.

B0221 H supports an affectionate Valentine-framed address: a heart-shaped chocolate for the manager, singing while thinking of him and a hoped-for flutter (P121-128). The reading leaves his response to the chocolate, any reciprocal confession and any agreed relationship outside the source, and B0237 credits him only with the encounter. One open-ended address cannot support simulating a romance.

B0221 H shows a professional problem (understanding a love song after coaching), peer counsel and the composer's acceptance, but the recording itself is elided and the evaluations are the speakers' own. B0244 503012301 shows her negotiate qualified participation in a magazine feature after Player acknowledges she may refuse, but no staff meeting, interview or production follows. E's staging idea is unrealized, and B0237's MC familiarity is her self-report. No working procedure is observed, so a professional scenario would be invention.

known_limits.statement: The eleven sources are independent conditional occurrences with no total chronology or year; menu, catalog or execution order cannot order them, B0244's Event family has no placement relative to Main or other families, cross-case comparisons are thematic, and B0237's Ferb report is a bounded relative-time statement, not a shared calendar.
No vocal performance, lyrics or CM-song sound appears in H; the composer's and manager's praise are their own evaluations, not a heard performance.
The piggyback acceptance in B0221 A and the pedicure over the manager's attempted escape in B are separate cases; neither supplies general consent, and one cannot be transferred to the other.
The manager's response to the chocolate, eating, a reciprocal confession and an agreed relationship are outside H's ending and must not be supplied.
B0237 P19 retains earlier friends, seniors, juniors and acquaintances; Nanasta and the manager did not supply her first relationships.
The peers in B0232, Haru in B0221 G and the Nanasta celebrants in B0237 have no turns; their views reach the evidence only through Murasaki. Honoka, Miu and Player do speak in B0244 503012305.

The after-work drinks, mirror-ball staging, joint cleaning, pedicure-shop outing, lifetime-remembering commitment, the requested cat visit and Player's promised caution are proposals, promises or refusals, not completed acts; B0244 shows no staff meeting, published article or verified fan gain.

In B0244 503012304 she suggests the abandoned cat seemed like her and then refuses to explain (P12-13). The literal cat is distinct from her earlier stray-cat metaphor, and neither supplies an abandonment history, diagnosis or self-theory; the withheld meaning must not be filled in.
Her cat-visit refusal rests on a possible allergy in a child, not on any named person's diagnosis, and Player's acceptance is a local promise without shown implementation.
No performed voice, singing, music, loop movie or continuous runtime was heard or watched. Static sprites, the bar and studio backgrounds and the purple stand are not performances.

The earlier Murasaki readings (B0039, B0087, B0105, B0140, B0178) and her family-bar and work-strain states are not curated on this subject, so the readings' comparisons with them were not checked. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
Apart from an address form, a title and a few short quotations, the readings paraphrase Murasaki's Japanese, so self-reference and sentence endings are largely absent from the curated evidence.

dimensions.note: The cumulative interpretation is that Murasaki wants to be treated as an ordinary young woman and indulged (A:P1-P2, F:P4) while offering practical and material care (B, C, H), values a place through the people who share it (D:P3-P4) and is angry at her own failure to care for it (G:P3). The reading tests a bitter-persona inference against her sweet coffee (F:P3) and keeps care from excusing her command against escape (B:P3), but derives no conditional rules, and each address is a few pages to one interlocutor, so D is rejected.

The reading forbids ordering the occurrences. Her one developmental remark, that she once wanted only to sing and now thinks about making companions look beautiful (E:P4), is her own account, and the earlier readings that would locate it are not enrolled.

Located wording is limited to episode titles such as 色っぽくしたげる and 甘いのもちょうだい and short formal and disclosive turns that the reading paraphrases. The 30 voice references in A-G were not heard and H has no voice files, so no register analysis is in evidence.

Ordinary acts are located: accepting a piggyback (A:P3), a pedicure presented as finished (B:P4), an after-work invitation with a soft drink for herself (C:P3), sweet coffee she made (F:P1-P2), a request to clean the theatre together (G:P5), and chocolate preparation, tempering, mold choice, waiting and wrapping with Kazumi (H:P42-82). The completed evening, cleaning and eating are not shown, and no rule generalizes them.

A-G address the manager, with Haru present only through Murasaki's report (G:P2). H gives Kazumi, the unnamed composer and the manager their own turns, distinguishing a peer's qualified counsel, a professional's acceptance and the addressed person's reaction (H:P105-119). One story with three counterparts does not support recipient conditioning beyond E.

Interior states are spoken or reader-only: she cannot verbalize what love means (H:P14) or what making the chocolate felt like (H:P91-100), the parenthesized P99-100 thoughts are available to the reader but not to others, and she admits restless concern while waiting (H:P65-73). These are local to one story.

One located episode: after Haru's reported scolding she clarifies that she is angry at her own failure rather than the reprimand, says being called unexpectedly delicate hurts, and turns to a practical request to clean together (G:P1-P5). Haru's own words are absent, and one case supports only E.

The reading does not analyze ethical reasoning. Its point that care and affection do not make another person's assent unnecessary (B:P3) is the analyst's caution about her method, not her deliberation, and absence is not evidence about her ethics.

Play is located in the suggestive dyed-in-my-colour question redirected toward style (B:P1-P2), the closing declaration that he will have to spend the day barefoot (B:P4), the jukebox metaphor she calls youthful (D:P5) and the joke that a taste for bitter songs does not predict coffee (F:P3). Instances are brief and directed at the manager.

The family is complete: eight occurrences with exact scripts and hashes, all 124 Japanese and name records and 169 full objects read, 19 static outputs and 10 backgrounds viewed, and 159 context rows read. It remains seven short addresses and one story; earlier readings are not enrolled, and no performed audio or runtime was reviewed.

Affirmative local limits are located: her sweet coffee against a bitter-song persona (F:P3), her command not to run away during the pedicure (B:P3), her skipped theatre cleaning (G:P2), her inability to put love or the chocolate-making feeling into words (H:P14, H:P91-100), and Kazumi's keeping her own answer secret (H:P39). These are single-occurrence facts.
No chronology, calendar year or unlock level orders the occurrences; the Valentine event is undated, and the age statement is local self-account.
